This Bail Application is filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS),
2023.
2.
The petitioner is the accused No.1 in Crime No.636/2025 of Thodupuzha Police Station.

The above case is registered against the petitioner and other accused for the offences punishable under Sections 316(2) (406 of IPC), 318(4) (420 of IPC), 351(2) (506 of IPC), 308(2) (384 0f IPC) and 3(5)
(34 of IPC) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.
3.

The prosecution case is that on 17.01.2025, the petitioner along with three other persons went to the Jewellery shop run by the defacto complainant and allegedly purchased gold ornaments and to clear the liability issued a cheque for an amount of Rs.7,37,468/-.

It is further alleged that on 28.01.2025, the petitioner threatened the defacto complainant and 2025:KER:33658 BAIL APPL.
NO.6017 OF 2025 obtained the cheques leaves.
4. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
The petitioner is a former MLA and a political leader.
Accused Nos.2 & 3 requested the petitioner to introduce them in a Jewellery shop to purchase gold ornaments on credit.
The Jewellery shop owner obtained the cheque leaves from the petitioner and the other accused and handed over the gold ornaments.
The petitioner has not intentionally committed any offence.
5. The case diary is made available.
Perused the case diary.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that as a social worker, the petitioner only introduced the other accused to the Jewellery owner and that he has not committed any offences.
8. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application of the petitioner.
On a perusal of the materials placed before this Court, this Court is of the view that the elements of false implication cannot be ruled out.
Essentially the transaction alleged is of civil nature.

10. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of this case, this Court is of the view that the petitioner has established a prima facie case for getting the benefits contained in Section 482 of the BNSS.
(i) The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 25.05.2025 and shall undergo interrogation.

(ii) The investigating officer is directed to release the petitioner on bail, in the event of his arrest, on his executing bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum.
(iii) The petitioner shall co-
operate with the Investigation agency.
2025:KER:33658 BAIL APPL. NO.6017 OF 2025 (iv) The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.
(v) The petitioner shall not influence the witnesses in this case or tamper with the evidence.
